title: What Contradictions Meet
description: What Contradictions Meet in Tonic Solfa to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR), doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book II, hymn 26, “Travailing in birth for souls. Gal 4:19”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Hallelujah Metre (6.6.6.6.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR); any other Hallelujah Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: What con-tra-dic-tions meet In min-is-ters' em-ploy! It is a bit-ter sweet, A sor-row full of joy: No oth-er post af-fords a place For e-qual hon-or, or dis-grace!

lines: No other post affords a place
To hearts as hard as steel?
Or who can tell the pleasures felt,
When stubborn hearts begin to melt?
They pray and strive, their rest departs,
Till Christ be formed in sinners hearts.
Too oft they find their hopes deceived,
Then, how their inmost souls are grieved!
To find the fruit of all their cares.
On what has now been sown
To make it spring and grow:
Do thou the gracious harvest raise,
And thou, alone, shalt have the praise.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
